docs.title: 1. Getting Started
docs.text: Thank you for purchasing an EasyRoll Smart Blind. Follow this guide and anyone can install and use it with ease.

docs.title: Check the Contents
docs.text: Item Description Main unit — DIY motor unit The motor unit that goes inside the blind 01 Remote (optional) Not included with EasyRoll IoT 02 Adapter (12V) For power supply 03 Power connection cable Connects blind to blind · Extends the adapter cable length 04 QR code card Same as the QR code on the motor unit — used during device registration

docs.title: Before Assembly, Check That the Motor Works
docs.text:
Before installing it into the blind, do a quick check that the motor unit runs properly.

  1. Connect the adapter (power connection cable) to the motor unit.
  2. Plug the adapter into an outlet.
  3. If the motor moves back and forth (up and down) a little and then stops → it's working!

👉 When you connect power, the motor makes a tiny rotation in both directions. This isn't a fault — it's a "working properly" greeting motion.

If you see this motion, the motor itself is fine

If registration or control doesn't work afterward, it's likely not a motor fault but a Wi-Fi / communication issue. See the Troubleshooting FAQ.

  • Once confirmed, unplug the power and move on to 1-1. Installation Guide (Assembly).
  • If there's no response at all, recheck the adapter and cable connections, and if it still doesn't work, contact the Customer Center.

docs.title: 2-1. Upper/Lower Limit Setup
docs.text:
Be sure to complete the Upper/Lower Limit Setup for your blind. This is the process of teaching the blind "how far up and how far down it should go." Only after this setup will it move precisely to the position you want (%), and will saved positions (M1–M3) and alarms work correctly.

After registration, the guide screen below appears. Tap [No, I want to set it up!] to start right away.

💡 The on-screen note "Settings -> Device Management -> Specify top/bottom" is an old path. Today you'll find it under ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Top/Bottom limit setting].

Please read before you start

In Setting mode, the blind moves without any limit stops. Be sure to press ■ Stop before it reaches the end. If it keeps winding, the blind can be damaged, so please make sure you understand the steps below before proceeding.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
1. Before setup, lower the blind all the way down and then raise it back up.
  2. In Setting mode, move the blind to your desired "topmost" position → [Specify top]
  3. Then move it to your desired "bottommost" position → [Specify bottom]
    • ⚠️ Always specify the top first, then the bottom!
  4. If you have several blinds, use ◀ ▶ to switch between devices and repeat.

Good to know

  • To set it up later — tap the ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Top/Bottom limit setting]
  • If the direction is reversed — you can change it with [Change motor direction] on the screen.
  • If you re-set the upper limit — the lower limit and saved positions are automatically adjusted along with it. No need to set everything again.

docs.title: 2-2. Change Zone & Number
docs.text:
Use this feature to change the blind number you set during registration, or to move a blind to another zone.

Nothing to change? Move on to the next step

If you'll use it just as registered, go straight to 3. Basic Usage.

Tap the ⚙ (gear) next to the zone name → [Zone device settings], where all the organizing menus are gathered.

Task How Example Change blind numbers Zone device settings → Change blind numbers Living Room 1 / Living Room 2 Move to another zone Zone device settings → Move blind to another zone Living Room → Bedroom Rename a zone Zone device settings → Rename zone "Zone 1" → "Living Room"

docs.title: Checking device info
docs.text:
[Device info] in the same [Zone device settings] shows the status of each blind. The values you need for customer support or Home Assistant integration are here.

Item Contents Firmware The device software version currently installed (7. Device Update) Network Device IP · router ID/IP · Wi-Fi signal strength and channel · MAC Remote Registered remote ID · channel Home Assistant Connected (broker · account) / Not used / Not supported on this device

docs.title: 2. Register Device
docs.text: This is the step where you connect your blind to your home Wi-Fi (router) and to the app. You only need to do it once. (About 3 minutes)

docs.title: What You'll Need
docs.text:
• The EasyRoll app, logged in (see 1-2. Installing the App & Signing Up)
  • Your home Wi-Fi (router) name and password (it must be 2.4GHz — see below)
  • The blind's QR code

⚠️ Check these before registering (same as the in-app guidance)

  1. Blinds connect to 2.4GHz Wi-Fi only — if your router name ends in ...5G, choose the one without the 5G.
  2. Your router must have a password set.
  3. Turn off your phone's Bluetooth and smartwatch while registering.
  4. Don't keep Bluetooth devices close to the router.

docs.title: Registration Steps — Do Several at Once!
docs.text:
If you have multiple blinds, you can register them all at once, one zone (room) at a time.

① Get started — This is the first screen you see after logging in. Tap the [+ Add zone/device] button in the center to begin.

On the [Add device] screen, tap [Add new zone]. (To add blinds to a zone you already created, choose [Add existing zone] instead — it appears only once you have at least one zone.)

② Create a zone — Choose a zone (Living Room, Bedroom, etc.) and select the number of blinds you're installing.

③ Scan QR codes — Tap the blind illustrations on screen in order to photograph each device's QR code. (The number in the middle of each illustration becomes that blind's number — when you add to an existing zone, numbering continues from the first free number)

💡 If you don't have a QR code or scanning is difficult, you can use [No QR code?] at the bottom of the screen to search for and register nearby blinds.

The search list shows each device's signal strength (bars) and the last digits of its serial number. Stronger bars mean the device is closer to your phone, and matching the highlighted last digits with the device label (EZS…) makes it easy to tell which physical device is which.

④ Connect to Wi-Fi — After reviewing the notes, choose your home Wi-Fi from the list and enter the password.

⑤ Automatic registration — Your blinds connect automatically, one after another. (Preparing → Sending Wi-Fi info → Verifying device → Connected)

💡 Seeing "Waiting, will retry soon" partway through is normal. If the signal is briefly delayed, the app retries automatically — don't treat it as an immediate failure; just wait a moment.

💡 While registration is in progress, a [Stop registration] button appears below [Finish]. If one device keeps retrying and never finishes, tap it — devices already registered are kept, only the remaining ones stop, and you return to the main screen.

⑥ Registration complete!

💡 If you've finished registering but a device doesn't appear, try restarting the app.

Once registration is done, your blind is connected to your home Wi-Fi, so you can control it with the app even when you're away from home.

docs.title: When It's Not Working
docs.text:
Symptom Solution "Device could not join the Wi-Fi" appears / registration keeps failing The device couldn't join your home Wi-Fi — check that the router is 2.4GHz and the Wi-Fi password is correct / Check that the scanned QR code matches the device you're registering / Check that Bluetooth and smartwatch are turned off / Move the phone and device closer to the router and retry "Waiting, will retry soon" appears It's retrying automatically after a brief delay. Wait a moment and it continues. If it keeps repeating, move your phone close to the device and check the 2.4GHz network and password One device keeps retrying and never finishes Tap [Stop registration] below the progress list. Devices already registered are kept; register the rest later (with [Add existing zone] if that zone already has a registered blind, otherwise [Add new zone]) Registration keeps dropping or is slow Keep your smartphone close to the blind while registering. If it's too far away, the connection may fail Device doesn't appear in the app after registration Fully close the app and restart it

For more detailed, symptom-by-symptom help, see the Troubleshooting FAQ.

docs.title: 1-2. Installing the App & Signing Up
docs.text: To control your blinds from your smartphone, you'll need the EasyRoll app. From install to login takes just 2 minutes.

docs.title: Installing the App
docs.text:
EasyRoll Smart Blind Look for this icon in your app store

Smartphone How to install Android Search "EasyRoll" on Google Play → Install iPhone Search "EasyRoll" on the App Store → Install

docs.title: Sign Up · Log In
docs.text:
The first time you open the app, a start screen appears. If you're new, tap [Create a username]; if you already have an account, tap [Login] next to "Already signed up?" at the bottom. Both screens offer social login buttons.

Method Description Social Login Android Google · Kakao · Naver / iPhone Kakao · Naver · Apple · Google — start right away with an account you already use (no separate password needed) Email Sign-up [Create a username] → [Sign up with EasyRoll] — sign up directly with an email + password

💡 When you first sign up, you'll select your region (country). Alarm and time features run according to that region's time.

Once you're logged in, it's time for the next step — registering your blind in the app.

docs.title: Controlling from the App
docs.text:
Button Action ⌃ Open Raises all the way to the top (tap briefly to move a little at a time) ⌄ Close Lowers all the way to the bottom (tap briefly to move a little at a time) ■ Stop Stops right where it is Blind card Tap — select which blind to control (you can select several)Press and hold the blind image, then drag up/down — release when "Release to move" appears to move to that position (%)Tap the % number — move just that blind to the position (%) you wantLong-press the name — open the [Device info] screen % Move the selected blinds to any position (%) — scroll the number or type it in (e.g. 30%)

💡 3-channel devices whose device ID starts with EZS11 don't support dragging the image or tapping the % number. For blinds shared with you, long-pressing the name doesn't open [Device info].

Icons at the top of the main screen

Icon What it does Replay the usage guide Manage Members — invite family or colleagues to share (Add Members) Alarms (schedules) (3-1. Alarm Settings) Settings menu

Good to know

  • Tap briefly to move a little, long-press to move all the way.
  • [Jog step] (levels 1–4) — adjusts how far it moves on a brief tap. The lower the number, the smaller and more precise the movement. (Handy for lining up combi blind patterns)
  • [Whole zone] toggle — when on, all blinds in that zone move together.
  • [Auto-Level] toggle — when you move several blinds together, it automatically aligns their heights (the bottom-bar line). For details, see 4. Using Multiple Blinds Together.

docs.title: Simplify the Screen — List View
docs.text:
Tap the ⌄ (arrow) next to a zone title to collapse the cards into a one-line summary list. Handy when you have many blinds.

💡 The list works just like the cards: tap to select, tap the % number to set the position (%) of just that blind, and long-press the name for [Device info]. (Dragging works on cards only.)

docs.title: Saving Frequently Used Positions (Memory)
docs.text:
You can save up to three (M1, M2, M3) frequently used heights (e.g. open halfway) and recall them in one tap.

  • Save — move to the height you want → long-press a memory button (M1–M3) → confirm save
  • Recall — tap a memory button briefly to move straight to that height

💡 The M1–M3 positions you've saved can also be used as-is in 3-1. Alarm Settings. (e.g. move to the M1 position at 7 a.m.)

docs.title: Settings Menu at a Glance (Menu ≡ → Settings)
docs.text: Menu What it does Change member information · Set language Account and app language Manage Members Invite family or colleagues to share (also opens from the 👥 icon at the top of the main screen) — see Add Members Zone & device management (on the screen, the next four rows — Add device through Change zone order · Move blind to another zone — are grouped under this heading) Add device Register an additional blind Up/down setting before device registration Set the upper/lower limits before registering in the app — your phone connects straight to the blind, no router needed Zone settings Manage devices by zone (upper/lower limits, Auto-Level, remote, Wi-Fi router, Home Assistant connection, updates, device info) — covered in each chapter Change zone order · Move blind to another zone Organize the order and grouping shown on the main screen App settings Set Triple shade mode, Push notification, Background color, and more Contact us · How to use Customer support, usage guides

docs.title: Good to Know
docs.text:
• If the blind snags on something while lowering, it stops automatically (motor protection). Clear the obstruction and run it again.
  • A slight movement each time the power is turned on is normal (an operation-check motion).

docs.title: 5. Using the Remote Control
docs.text: The remote control works even without WiFi (it uses a dedicated wireless signal). Even if your internet goes down, the remote always works.

docs.title: Remote Pairing (Channel Registration)
docs.text:
To use the remote, you need to register your blind to a remote channel. There are two ways to do this.

Register with the App (Recommended)Register Directly with the Remote (No App)

This is the easiest way — you just tap a channel on the app screen to assign it.

The device must be registered in the app first

Your blind must be registered in the app before you can register the remote through the app. If you haven't registered it yet, please complete 2. Register Device first. If you want to use the remote without registering in the app, see the [Register Directly with the Remote] tab.

Location: ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Register/Edit remote channel]

  1. Tap [Register/Edit remote channel] → [Register remote channel].
  2. Press the ■ Stop button on the remote once, then tap [I pressed the remote button] in the app.
    • Once the remote ID is recognized, the app moves on to the next step. If it doesn't, press the Stop button again and tap [I pressed the remote button] once more.
  3. Select the channel (1–5) to use for each blind, then tap [Register] to finish.

💡 To change a channel, go to [Register/Edit remote channel] → [Edit remote channel], pick the channel for each blind, and tap [Apply changes].

This is how to register using just the remote and the blind device, without the app.

docs.title: Registering one blind to channel 1
docs.text:
Left image = ① Hold [◀ Left] (1+ second) · Right image = ② Hold [■ Stop] for 5+ seconds

  1. Press and hold the [◀ Left] button on the remote (for at least 1 second).
  2. Press and hold the [■ Stop] button for at least 5 seconds.
    • The LEDs on all blind motors will blink.
  3. Firmly press and quickly release the reset button on the blind motor you want to assign to channel 1.
    • When the LED blinks rapidly several times, channel 1 is assigned!

docs.title: Registering channels 2–5
docs.text:
Only the number of short presses of the [▶ Right] button in step ① changes; everything else is the same.

Channel In step ① 1 Hold [◀ Left] only 2 Hold [◀ Left] + press [▶ Right] briefly once 3 Hold [◀ Left] + press [▶ Right] briefly twice 4 Hold [◀ Left] + press [▶ Right] briefly three times 5 Hold [◀ Left] + press [▶ Right] briefly four times

docs.title: Grouping several blinds on one channel (Group Registration)
docs.text:
If you register several blinds to one channel, they all move together on that channel. The method is the same — in step ③, just press the reset button on each of the blinds you want to group, one after another.

💡 Registration is retained even when the power is turned off.

docs.title: Getting to Know the Remote Buttons
docs.text:
Button Action ⌃ Up Short press = raises a set distance · Long press = raises all the way up ■ Stop Stops a moving blind ⌄ Down Short press = lowers a set distance · Long press = lowers all the way down ◀ ▶ Channel Select Short press [▶ Right] = moves in the order 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → ALLShort press [◀ Left] = moves in the order ALL → 5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1 (reverse)Hold [▶ Right] = selects all blinds · Hold [◀ Left] = selects blind 1 M Favorite Height (Memory) Long press = saves the current position · Short press = moves to the saved position Lamp Turns on each time you press the button (once for a short press, twice for a long press)

💡 When you select a channel, the selected blind moves slightly up and down to let you know.

docs.title: Controlling Several Blinds by Channel
docs.text:
Channel Action 1 – 5 Only the blinds registered to that channel operate ALL All registered blinds operate together

Example: Register 3 living room blinds to channels 1, 2, and 3 respectively → switch channels to control them one at a time. If you register several blinds to the same channel, they move together on that channel.

docs.title: When Things Don't Work
docs.text: Symptom Solution No response when pressed Check that the channel is correct → replace the battery → re-register One press moves a neighboring blind too Channels are registered with overlap — re-register each to a different channel Registration won't work Try again close to the device (1–2 m)

docs.title: 4. Using Multiple Blinds Together
docs.text: If you have installed several blinds, you can control them all at once by zone (room) and line up their heights neatly.

docs.title: Controlling a Whole Zone at Once
docs.text: On the main screen, turning on the [Whole zone] toggle selects that entire zone, and the [Select all] toggle on the control panel selects every blind on the screen.

docs.title: Lining Up Heights Neatly — Auto-Level
docs.text: When you raise or lower several blinds together in one zone and then press [Stop], this feature automatically lines up the heights of the blinds that moved, using either the highest one (when raising) or the lowest one (when lowering) as the reference.

docs.title: ① Turn It On First (once per zone)
docs.text:
Tap the ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Auto-Level] → set the zone you want to align to ON

💡 The [Auto-Level] toggle on the main-screen control panel turns it on or off for all zones at once. (Turning it off also clears the settings you made for each zone.) To use it only in certain zones, turn it on zone by zone under [Zone device settings] → [Auto-Level] above.

ℹ️ This setting is saved on this phone (app) only. Family members or other phones need to turn it on separately.

docs.title: ② Using It
docs.text:
In a zone where Auto-Level is on, after moving two or more blinds together:

Action Result [Stop] after raising The rest line up to the highest one [Stop] after lowering They line up to the lowest one Press and hold [Stop] for 1.5 seconds or longer An [Align to top] · [Align to bottom] · [Align to average] popup appears → they line up to the height you choose (highest · lowest · average height)

💡 Automatic alignment runs when you press [Stop] within 1 minute of pressing [Open] or [Close]. (Moves made with M1–M3 or % are not auto-aligned.) If the blinds stopped on their own before you pressed [Stop] (for example, after a short press that moved them only a little), press [Stop] once within 1 minute. (If you have already pressed [Stop] once, or more than 1 minute has passed, another short press of [Stop] does nothing.)

💡 Only the blinds that moved are aligned. (For example, if you raise and stop only 2 of 4 blinds, only those 2 are lined up.)

💡 Even when the blinds are different lengths, they are aligned so that the bottom bars actually end up level.

💡 To choose the alignment height yourself — keep holding [Stop] for 1.5 seconds or longer without letting go, and an [Align to top] · [Align to bottom] · [Align to average] popup appears. Pick one and the selected blinds line up neatly at that height. You can use this at any time, even if you haven't just moved them — simply select the blinds you want to align first. (If you let go before 1.5 seconds, no popup appears and they align by movement direction as usual.)

ℹ️ The popup appears only when there is something to align — that is, when you have selected two or more blinds at different heights in a zone where Auto-Level is on.

ℹ️ Auto-Level works by adjusting after the blinds stop, so you may see a slight correction movement at the end right after stopping. This is normal.

docs.title: If a Blind Has a Weak WiFi Signal
docs.text:
A blind far from your router may respond slowly because of a weak signal.

  • It helps to move the router closer to the blinds, or to add a WiFi booster (extender).
  • If just one blind is repeatedly slow or keeps dropping out, check the signal strength at that location.

docs.title: Troubleshooting FAQ
docs.text: When something goes wrong, check the items below in order. Most issues are resolved within 1–2 minutes.

docs.title: First of All — Look at the LED
docs.text: LED Pattern Status Fix Off + working normally Normal — Blinks once every 3 seconds Internet is fine, but it is retrying the server connection Leave it and it will recover automatically (usually within a few minutes). Remote and buttons work normally in the meantime 1 second on + 1 second off, repeating Cannot connect to WiFi (router) Check the router's power/distance → if you changed routers, see Changing Your Router 3 quick blinks + pause, repeating Server registration has been lost Re-register with the app (2. Registering Your Device) — it sometimes recovers automatically Won't turn on at all, unresponsive Power problem Check the adapter/outlet, reconnect the power

docs.title: Q. The app can't control it (but the remote works)
docs.text: This is an internet/server connection problem. The blind tries to recover on its own, so wait a few minutes. If it still doesn't work: ① check that your home internet is working → ② restart the router → ③ reconnect the blind's power.

docs.title: Q. I changed my WiFi router / I changed the password
docs.text: See 6. Changing Your Router. (If the new router has the same name and password, it reconnects automatically.)

docs.title: Q. The slider % position is off / it only goes to 0 and 100
docs.text: The Upper/Lower Limit Setup has not been done. Please complete 2-1. Upper/Lower Position Setup.

docs.title: Q. It stops partway while going down
docs.text: If there is an object in the way, it stops automatically to protect the motor. Remove whatever is blocking it (a drying rack, a plant pot, etc.) and run it again.

docs.title: Q. It moves slightly every time I turn the power on
docs.text: This is normal. When you connect the power, the motor performs a check by rotating a tiny bit left and right. 👉 If you see this movement, it means the motor itself is fine. If control still doesn't work, it is most likely a WiFi/communication problem rather than a motor failure.

docs.title: Q. I want to delete a device from the app
docs.text:
Tap the ⚙ next to the zone name → [Delete device] → select the blind to remove → [Delete selected]. (To use the device again, re-register it via 2. Registering Your Device.) Deleting also erases the device's WiFi settings and restarts it in setup mode (the top/bottom position settings are kept). If the device was off (offline) when you deleted it, press and hold the button on the device body for 5 seconds or more to reset it before registering it again. If the device was connected to Home Assistant, deleting it in the app also cleans up its Home Assistant registration automatically. (Move / Remove Device)

💡 If you only want to move a blind to another zone, don't delete it — use ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Move blind to another zone] instead. (2-2. Change Zone & Number)

docs.title: Q. I want to start over from scratch (factory reset)
docs.text:
Press and hold the button on the device body for 5 seconds or more. The WiFi/server connection info (including Home Assistant settings) is erased and the device goes back to the waiting-for-registration (setup) state. The top/bottom positions and the paired remote are kept → start again from 2. Registering Your Device.

💡 To move the device to a different account, first delete it in the app of the original account. A button reset alone doesn't release the account registration, so registering it with another account shows "This device is registered to the account ○○. Please delete it from that account first."

docs.title: Q. Where can I see the device IP or firmware version?
docs.text: Tap the ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Device info] to see the device IP, router, Wi-Fi signal, firmware version, remote and Home Assistant status. (2-2. Change Zone & Number)

docs.title: Q. Can I use it with Home Assistant?
docs.text: Yes. You can keep using the EasyRoll app and connect to Home Assistant at the same time (Hybrid). Tap the ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] — see the Home Assistant Integration Guide for details. (Firmware V3.2.0 or later)

docs.title: If That Still Doesn't Solve It
docs.text:
Customer Center 031-358-1016 · Weekdays 09:00 – 18:00

Website easyroll.kr · Community → Q&A board

When you contact us, telling us the name on the device label (EZS...) and the LED status helps us assist you much faster. The motor unit comes with a 2-year free warranty.

docs.title: 3-1. Alarm Setup (Automatic at a Set Time)
docs.text: You can have your blind open and close automatically at set times. (For example, open at 7 AM on weekdays.)

docs.title: Adding an Alarm
docs.text:
1. At the top of the app's main screen, tap 🕐 → on the Alarm list screen, tap [+] at the top right
  2. Select blind — tap Select blinds to expand it, then tap a zone name and check the blinds.
    • Tap the check on the right of a zone to select the whole zone.
    • You can mix blinds from several zones.
    • Nothing is selected at first. You can tap [Save] only after choosing blinds.
  3. Select a time
  4. Select a blind position
  5. Select the days → [Save]
Item Description Time What hour and minute it runs (or based on sunrise/sunset — see below) Blind Position Top / Bottom / M1–M3 (saved positions) / a custom % Days The days to repeat Blind Which zone/blind it applies to (pick any mix of zones and blinds)

You can turn alarms you've created on and off with a switch in the list.

docs.title: Match It to Sunrise / Sunset (Sunrise & Sunset Alarms)
docs.text:
Instead of a fixed time, you can also set it based on sunrise (when the sun comes up) or sunset (when the sun goes down). It follows along automatically even as the times change with the seasons.

When adding an alarm, choose from [Time | Sunrise | Sunset] → then specify [minutes before / minutes after] the reference point.

Example) Close 30 minutes after sunset · Open 10 minutes before sunrise

💡 It runs based on the sunrise/sunset times of your region (the region you selected at sign-up).

docs.title: Editing & Deleting Alarms
docs.text:
• Turn on/off — the switch next to the alarm in the list
  • Edit — select the alarm in the list → change its details
  • Delete — press and hold the alarm card and a delete screen appears. Select the alarm to remove and delete it.

⚠️ Alarms require an internet connection. At the set time, the server sends the command to the blind, so the blind must be connected to the internet (home WiFi) for it to work.

💡 Alarms work even when your phone is turned off (because the server sends them). However, if the blind is offline, it may miss the action at that time.

docs.title: 6. Changing the Wi-Fi Router
docs.text: If you've replaced your router with a new one, or your Wi-Fi name or password has changed, your blind can't connect to the internet. When this happens, just re-enter the updated Wi-Fi information on the device.

docs.title: When You'll Need This
docs.text:
• When you've replaced your internet router with a new one
  • When you've changed your Wi-Fi name or password
  • When you've moved and are using a different router

If the new router keeps the same name and password, it reconnects on its own, so this process isn't needed.

docs.title: How to Change It
docs.text:
1. ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Change Wi-Fi]

  2. Pick the option that fits your situation.

    • [I have not changed the router yet] — the device is still connected to the old router (the blind still moves from the app). Choose the devices to reset and tap [Reset Wi-Fi and continue]; the device switches to setup mode and then connects to the new router. If you haven't swapped the router yet, this is the most reliable way.
    • [I already changed the router] — you've already switched to the new router and the device dropped off. → See When Only the Router Changed and the Device Dropped Off below.
  3. Follow the guidance → enter the new Wi-Fi name and password
  4. Wait a moment for the connection to the new router to complete

⚠️ On a device that also uses HA (Hybrid), resetting with [I have not changed the router yet] also clears the HA connection settings. After connecting to the new router, run ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again.

💡 The [Up/down setting before device registration] option in the same menu is for when you want to set the upper/lower limits first, without a Wi-Fi connection.

💡 The new Wi-Fi must also be 2.4GHz. (not ...5G)

docs.title: When Only the Router Changed and the Device Dropped Off (Automatic AP Mode)
docs.text:
If you only changed the router and the device can't find its old Wi-Fi, just wait a moment — the device returns to setup mode (AP) on its own. (firmware V2.9.7 or later) When an EZS... network reappears in your phone/PC Wi-Fi list, it's ready.

💡 You can check the firmware version while the device is connected: ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Device info] → Firmware.

  1. Wait 1–2 minutes until the device Wi-Fi (EZS...) appears in the list. (Don't unplug it — a power cycle restarts the attempts and makes it take longer.)
    • If the device runs firmware older than V2.9.7, or EZS... still hasn't appeared after 2–3 minutes, hold the button on the unit for 5 seconds to reset its Wi-Fi settings. When EZS... appears shortly after, continue from step 2 below in the same way. (The registration and upper/lower limits are kept. However, a button reset clears the HA connection settings, so on a Hybrid device run [Home Assistant] in the app again after connecting.)

  2. Enter the new router (Wi-Fi) info according to how you used the device.

    • Standard (app only) or Hybrid (app + HA together) device — in the EasyRoll app, zone ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Change Wi-Fi] → [I already changed the router] → select the device → follow the guidance to enter the new Wi-Fi name and password
      • The app joins the device Wi-Fi (EZS...) by itself, so you don't need to connect to it on your phone. (On iPhone, you scan the device QR code instead of searching nearby.)
      • When the device returned to setup mode on its own, a Hybrid device keeps its saved HA settings too. (If the HA machine's IP also changed with the new router, run ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again in the app with the new address after connecting.)
    • HA-only device — use a browser. The device's own setup pages are in Korean only, so the Korean labels are shown with English in parentheses.
      • In your phone/PC Wi-Fi settings, connect to EZS....
        • The device Wi-Fi password is u67184 + the last 3 digits of the device name. (e.g. name EZS...123 → u67184123)
      • Enter 192.168.4.1 in the address bar (Google Chrome recommended) → [Home Assistant] → enter the new Wi-Fi + HA broker info → [저장하고 연결] (Save and Connect) → for details, see Method ②-B in HA Integration · 2. Connecting the Device
      • Skip [⚙ 상/하단 설정] (Upper/Lower Limit Setup) on the first screen. The upper/lower limits are still saved.

    ⚠️ Don't save a Hybrid device from the browser's [Home Assistant] screen. Saving there switches it to HA only, and app control stops. Always change it from the app.

  3. Wait a moment and it reconnects to the new router automatically.

If you can't use the app — enter the new Wi-Fi with the browser's [HTTP] (Standard / Hybrid devices)

Use the app whenever you can. Use this method only when the app isn't available.

Devices with firmware older than V2.9.7 don't have the first screen below. Connect your phone/PC to the EZS... Wi-Fi, enter 192.168.4.1:25867/router in the address bar, and continue from step 2.

  1. Connect your phone/PC to the EZS... Wi-Fi, then enter 192.168.4.1 in the address bar → [HTTP]

  2. Enter Router SSID (the new Wi-Fi name) and Router PW (its password).

  3. Be sure to tick 서버세션ON (Server session ON). If you leave it unticked, you can no longer control the blind from the app.

  4. [등록하기] (Register) → tap OK on the pop-up → it's done when SUCCESS appears (this can take up to 1 minute).

    It's fine if the page just keeps loading. If EZS... disappears from the Wi-Fi list after about a minute and the blind moves from the app, it has worked.

💡 This screen automatically removes any spaces from the Wi-Fi name and password, and accepts up to 30 characters. If your name or password contains spaces or is longer than 30 characters, this method won't connect — use the app instead.

💡 This method also keeps a Hybrid device's HA settings.

Upper/lower limits and the current position are kept

You only need to re-enter the router (and HA) info — no need to set the limits again.

docs.title: When It's Not Working
docs.text: Symptom Solution Still no connection after changing Double-check the new Wi-Fi password → try again Blind is unresponsive Unplug the blind, plug it back in, and try again after 1 minute (but don't unplug it while you're waiting for EZS... to appear) Still not working Hold the button on the unit for 5 seconds to reset its Wi-Fi settings, then reconnect with the app's [Change Wi-Fi] → [I already changed the router] (the registration and limits are kept; the HA connection settings are cleared, so if the device used HA, connect it again with HA Integration · 2. Connecting the Device)

docs.title: 7. Device Update
docs.text: Every now and then a new-feature or stability update is released. You can easily update to the latest version in the app.

docs.title: How to Update
docs.text:
1. Tap the ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Firmware update]
  2. If you see "Update available", tap [Update] for each device, or [Update all] (when there are 2 or more devices)
  3. ⚠️ Do not turn off the power while it's in progress. (About 1–2 minutes; briefly offline during that time)
  4. When finished, the blind restarts → done!
Display Meaning Up to date next to the version · gray [Up to date] button Already latest — nothing to do Update available next to the version · [Update] button Tap to update to the latest Current: — (no label) The version hasn't been read yet — check that the device is online, then reopen the screen

⚠️ Cautions during the update

  • Do not turn off or unplug the power while it's in progress.
  • The blind must be connected to the internet (your home Wi-Fi).
  • A brief unresponsive moment is normal — it restarts automatically when done.

💡 Updates aren't mandatory, but they're recommended since they include new features and stability improvements.

💡 Home Assistant Hybrid integration (use alongside the app) requires firmware V3.2.0 or later. Check the current version under [Zone device settings] → [Device info] → Firmware.

docs.title: Add Members (Share with Family & Colleagues)
docs.text: With a single invite code, you can invite family or colleagues to control your blinds together. You can share a whole zone, or pick individual blinds one by one.

docs.title: Good to know first
docs.text:
• You can open Manage Members straight from the 👥 icon at the top of the main screen (next to the 🕐 alarm icon). It's the same screen as menu ≡ (Settings screen) → [Manage Members].
  • Members can only see and control the zones and blinds the owner allows.
  • Members can also create schedules (alarms) — they appear as "Created by ○○" in the list.
  • You can invite up to 5 members.
  • The invite code is 6 digits and works once, within 10 minutes.
  • Only the device owner (the inviter) can connect or disconnect Home Assistant. Member accounts don't see that menu. (Home Assistant integration)
  • SmartThings and Google Home can also be linked only with the owner's account. If you link with a member account, the blinds shared with you won't appear. (SmartThings · Google Home)

docs.title: ① Invite a member (blind owner)
docs.text:
1. Tap 👥 at the top of the main screen to open the Manage Members screen (or menu ≡ (Settings screen) → [Manage Members])

  2. [+ Invite]

  3. Choose the invite type — Family or Colleague

  4. Select zones to share

    • Turn on Whole zone to share every blind in that zone (including blinds added later)
    • Or tap the arrow (>) on the right of a zone to pick individual blinds (N/M selected)

  5. [Create invite code] → a 6-digit code and QR appear

  6. Send it with [Send code by text or messenger]

💡 The code is valid once, for 10 minutes. If it expired, tap [Create new code].

docs.title: ② Accept an invite (invited person)
docs.text:
1. Sign in to the EasyRoll app (if you don't have it, install & sign up first)
  2. Tap 👥 at the top of the main screen → [Enter invite code] (or menu ≡ (Settings screen) → [Manage Members] → [Enter invite code])

  3. Enter the 6-digit code you received or [Scan QR code] — it connects automatically (if it doesn't, tap [Connect] at the bottom)

  4. Once connected, the shared zone appears on your main screen labeled "Shared · ○○".

⚠️ If the code doesn't work — it may be expired (over 10 minutes), entered incorrectly, or it's your own code (which can't be used). After several failures, try again later.

docs.title: Using it together
docs.text:
Role Can do Member Control allowed zones/blinds · create schedules (alarms) Owner Revoke access · remove members anytime

💡 A member's schedules appear as "Created by ○○" in the list.

⚠️ When you revoke, unshare, or remove, the schedules that member created for that blind/zone are deleted together.

docs.title: Managing (blind owner)
docs.text:
Tap 👥 at the top of the main screen (the Manage Members screen) and select a member to see their Allowed zones and [Remove member].

To do How Turn off one zone In the member's Allowed zones, uncheck that zone → [Confirm] Take back one blind In the member's Allowed zones, tap the arrow (>) on the right of the zone, uncheck the blind → [Confirm] Remove a member Select the member → [Remove member]

💡 If the zone is shared as a Whole zone, you can't turn off just one blind. Turn off the zone first (the member's schedules for that zone are deleted), then pick only the blinds to keep.

⚠️ In every case, the related schedules that member created are deleted together.

docs.title: Leaving a share (invited person)
docs.text:
Tap 👥 at the top of the main screen → in Shared with me, tap [Leave].

After leaving, you can no longer control that zone, and the schedules you made for it are deleted.

docs.title: DIY Motor Unit Assembly
docs.text: This is the process of attaching the motor unit to the blind's head rail. All you need is a Phillips screwdriver.

docs.title: Please Read Before Assembly & Installation
docs.text:
Pre-Installation Checklist

  • First roll the blind all the way up, then begin assembly.
  • By default, viewed from inside the room, the motor is assembled on the right side of the blind.
    • If you install it on the left side, after assembly you must go to the app's Upper/Lower Limit Setup page and press the [Motor Direction] button to change the motor direction. (See 2-1. Upper/Lower Position Setup.)
  • Do not remove the cap on the motor unit shown in the photo below. Assemble it with the cap left in place.
  • Have ready the QR code card included with each motor. (Not applicable to EasyRoll Lite.)
    • If you are installing two or more blinds, it helps to write each blind's location or number (name) on its card so the QR code cards don't get mixed up!
    • It is the same as the QR code attached to the lower right of the motor unit.

docs.title: Assembly Steps
docs.text:
Tap a photo to view it larger.

1. Loosen the screw on the head rail's side cap. (※ The default is right-side assembly — for left-side installation, see the checklist above.)

2. Open the side cap and lay the head rail down on the floor.

3. Remove the blind cord.

4. Fit the head rail's side cap into the grooved slot on the side of the motor unit.

※ If there is play because the size doesn't quite fit: add a 'bushing' first, then attach the motor unit.

Select the tab that matches your type of head rail:

Box-Type Head RailOpen-Type Head Rail

Box-Type · Adding a Bushing When There's Play

＋ Insert the bushing so it forms a plus (＋) shape.

Open-Type · Adding a Bushing When There's Play

✕ Insert the bushing at the side cap insertion point so it forms a cross (✕) shape.

5. First, check the shape of your blind's pipe.

  • Pipe Type A → position A on the motor unit
  • Pipe Type B → position B on the motor unit

※ A/B is marked on the motor unit.

6. Turn the pipe you identified to match position A/B on the motor unit, then push the motor unit into the pipe. (※ Do not remove the motor's cap! Insert it with the cap left in place.)

7. Fit the idler into the pipe too, matching its shape (turning it as you go).

8. Stand the head rail you laid down back into position and close the side cap.

9. Fasten it with the screw. — Motor assembly complete! (※ Don't over-tighten the screw! It causes the motor to slow down.)

Install the blind only after you have also checked the power connection below.

※ Be sure to plug the adapter (power plug) into the outlet only after all installation is complete.

docs.title: How to Connect the Power
docs.text:
Select the tab that matches the number of blinds you are installing.

Installing 1 BlindInstalling 2 or More on a Connected Window

Connection Layout

  1. Connect the adapter to ①.
  2. Route ② up onto the head rail or fix it as far away from the blind fabric as possible. (※ Do not remove the protective cap!)
    • If it touches the fabric, static electricity builds up and causes malfunctions.

Connection Layout

  1. Connect the adapter to ①. (※ Connect it to the blind nearest the outlet.)
  2. Remove the protective cap on ② and connect the power connection cable to ② and ③. (※ Do not remove the one protective cap that remains after connecting!)
  3. Route the connection points up onto the head rail or fix them as far away from the blind fabric as possible.
    • If they touch the fabric, static electricity builds up and causes malfunctions.

Outlet Position · Cable Management

  • The outlet can be on either the left or the right side. Just connect the adapter to the motor unit nearest the outlet.
  • The adapter comes in a standard 1.2 m length, and you can extend it with a power connection cable.
  • A 5 m power connection cable comes in the basic package that contains the adapter, and a 3 m cable comes with each additional motor.
  • Manage the cables by routing them up above the head rail or toward the back!

For a combi blind, only loosen the screw fixed to the bottom bar slightly! If it is too tight, the tube can't rotate, which causes static electricity and malfunctions.

After installing the blind, you must register the product in the mobile app for it to work!

Once installation is finished, continue from 1-2. Installing the App & Signing Up.

docs.title: Google Home Integration
docs.text: Connect your EasyRoll Smart Blind to Google Home to operate it by voice with "Hey Google" on Google Nest speakers, Nest Hub displays and Android phones, and add it to Routines in the Google Home app so it moves automatically.

docs.title: Supported features
docs.text:
Feature In Google Home Open · Close Voice / Google Home app device card / Routines Any position (%) "Open the blind to 30%", "Open the blind halfway" — or use the slider (100% = fully open, Google convention) Position display The Google Home card shows a position, but it's the position last set through Google — after moving the blind with the EasyRoll app, the remote or an alarm (schedule) it may differ from the real position, and the blind is not shown as "offline" even when its power is off. Check the EasyRoll app for the exact status Routines Open in a "Good morning" routine, close in a bedtime routine, follow sunrise/sunset, etc.

⚠️ A "stop" voice command is not supported. To stop a moving blind, use ■ Stop in the EasyRoll app or on the remote.

docs.title: What You'll Need
docs.text:
• An account with your blind registered in the EasyRoll app (Register Device completed)
  • Connect with the account that registered (owns) the blinds — blinds shared with you as a member are not linked.
  • The Google Home app installed on your smartphone + signed in with your Google account
  • The blind connected to the internet (home Wi-Fi) — the Google Home integration works through the EasyRoll server
  • For accurate position (%) commands, the blind's upper/lower limits must be set (2-1. Upper/Lower Limit Setup)

docs.title: Connecting (One-Time Setup)
docs.text:
1. Google Home app → [＋] at the top right → [＋ Device]
  2. At the bottom of the QR code screen, tap [＋ Add another way] → under Search for brand or device, search for "EasyRoll"
  3. Log in with your EasyRoll account
  4. When your registered blinds appear in Google Home, assign them to a room (e.g. Living Room) and you're done!

💡 All blinds registered in the EasyRoll app are added to Google Home at once (only blinds registered to your own account — shared blinds are not included). If a blind you registered later doesn't show up, say "Hey Google, sync my devices" or refresh the link in the Google Home app.

💡 Give the blind a short name (e.g. "Living Room Blind") so voice commands are recognized easily. You can rename it in the device settings of the Google Home app.

docs.title: How You Can Use It
docs.text: Method Example Voice commands "Hey Google, open the living room blind" / "Close the blind" / "Open the blind halfway" / "Open the blind to 30%" By room With several blinds in one room, "Hey Google, close all the living room blinds" moves them all at once Google Home app · Nest Hub Open/close and position slider on the device card Routines Open the blinds in a "Good morning" routine, close them in a "Good night" routine, close all when leaving home, follow sunrise/sunset times

docs.title: When Things Don't Work
docs.text:
Symptom Solution EasyRoll doesn't appear in search Update the Google Home app to the latest version and try again Connected but the device doesn't show Check that you signed in with the owner account that registered the blinds (blinds shared with you as a member don't appear) → check in the EasyRoll app that the blind is properly registered and online → "Hey Google, sync my devices" Voice commands don't respond Check the device name (the name you call it in Google Home) — use a short, easy-to-say name that doesn't clash with a room name "Set the blind to 50%" doesn't work The blind's upper/lower limits aren't set → 2-1. Upper/Lower Limit Setup The position in Google Home doesn't match the blind The Google Home card shows the position last set through Google, so after moving the blind with the EasyRoll app, the remote or an alarm (schedule) it may look different from the real position. Check the EasyRoll app for the exact position. (Google Home uses 100% = fully open, the same as the EasyRoll app) It doesn't operate Check that the blind is online (FAQ) → disconnect the link and reconnect

docs.title: EasyRoll × Home Assistant Integration Guide
docs.text: Connecting your EasyRoll Smart Blind to Home Assistant lets you control it directly at home without the cloud, and use it in HA automations (sunrise/sunset, temperature triggers, etc.). We recommend the Hybrid setup — keep the EasyRoll app and connect HA in addition: even if the internet goes down, HA can still control it locally, and even if HA is off you keep control via the app as long as the internet is connected.

docs.text: Step Description 1. Getting Started · Requirements Integration method · Mosquitto broker 2. Connecting the Device ① From the app (Hybrid) ★Recommended · ② Device setup page by typing the IP 3. Using It in HA Cards · position slider · automation YAML examples 4. Advanced Commands Direct MQTT control Move / Remove Device Deleting in the app cleans up HA automatically · HA-only: EZS_HARESET$ 5. docs.text:
1. Install the Mosquitto broker add-on in HA → check the requirements
  2. Register the device with the EasyRoll app (skip if already in use) → Register Device
  3. In the app, tap ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] → select devices + enter the broker info → [Connect] → details

  • Automatic registration (MQTT Discovery) — no manual YAML required
  • Automatic online/offline status
  • App + HA at the same time (Hybrid) — control from both the EasyRoll app and HA simultaneously. Even if the internet goes down, HA can still control it locally, and even if HA is off you keep control via the app as long as the internet is connected. (Firmware V3.2.0 or later)

For general usage, see the User Manual.
