docs.title: 1. Getting Started — Home Assistant Integration Requirements
docs.text: The EasyRoll Smart Blind can connect directly to Home Assistant (HA). Once connected, you can control the blind from your HA dashboard and use it in HA automations (sunrise/sunset, temperature triggers, etc.).

docs.title: How does it work?
docs.text:
[Home Assistant] ←── home network (MQTT) ──→ [Blind]

  • This is a local connection that does not go through the cloud — it works at home even when the internet is down.
  • It uses HA's MQTT integration, and the blind registers automatically (no code to write).

There are two connection modes. Unless you have a specific reason, Hybrid is recommended.

Mode Description Hybrid (app + HA together) ★Recommended Keeps the EasyRoll server connection and connects to HA in addition. The two are independent, so even if the internet goes down, HA can still control it locally, and even if HA is off you keep control via the app as long as the internet is connected. After registering in the app, connect a whole zone at once from [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] in the app. (Firmware V3.2.0 or later) HA only Connects to HA only; EasyRoll app control stops. For running without the app, or on older firmware (V2.9.8+). Set up on the device setup page (type the IP directly)

docs.title: Requirements Checklist
docs.text: Item Description Home Assistant Installed and running (HA OS, container, etc. — any type) MQTT broker The HA Mosquitto broker add-on is recommended — see below for installation MQTT user account One HA user (e.g. easyroll1) — the blind logs in with this account Same network The blind and HA must be on the same Wi-Fi router EasyRoll app Latest version (includes the Hybrid connect menu) — signed in as the device owner Blind firmware Hybrid: V3.2.0 or later · HA only: V2.9.8 or later — check in the app's device info, update via 7. Device Update

docs.title: Installing the Mosquitto broker
docs.text: If you don't have an MQTT broker yet, install it as an HA add-on. (Skip this if you already use one.)

docs.title: ① Install the add-on
docs.text:
1. In the HA left menu, go to Settings → Apps (or Add-ons, depending on your version).
  2. Open the [Add-on Store] at the bottom right.
  3. Type mosquitto in the search box to find Mosquitto broker.
  4. Click [Install]. (Takes 1–2 minutes.)

docs.title: ② Startup settings
docs.text:
Once installed, configure it in the Controls area on the right of the add-on's [Info] tab.

  1. Click [Start] to run it. (If it's already running, you'll see Stop / Restart buttons.)
  2. Turning on the following two options keeps it stable:
    • Start on boot — the broker starts automatically when HA powers on
    • Watchdog — automatically restarts the broker if it stops
  3. When the status at the top left shows Running, everything is fine.

💡 The host name core-mosquitto at the bottom right of the same screen is used as the broker address later, when you manually add the MQTT integration.

💡 You can leave Auto update off. (Update manually whenever you like.)

docs.title: ③ Check the ports (leave the defaults as-is)
docs.text:
At the top of the add-on, the [Configuration] tab → the Network section at the bottom already has the ports configured.

Port Purpose 1883 Normal MQTT — the port the blind uses 1884 MQTT over WebSocket 8883 Normal MQTT with SSL 8884 MQTT over WebSocket with SSL

💡 The EasyRoll Smart Blind uses 1883 only. Unless you have a specific reason, leave the defaults as-is.

Don't touch the other settings

The SSL · Certificate/Private Key · Log Types · Customize and other options on the same [Configuration] tab are not needed for EasyRoll integration. Leave them at their defaults.

In particular, turning on Require Client Certificate will prevent the blind from connecting to the broker.

docs.title: ④ Create the MQTT account the blind will use
docs.text:
Mosquitto logs in with an HA user account. Create one dedicated account for the blind.

  1. Settings → Users (People/Users, depending on your version) → [Add user]
  2. Choose a name and username. (e.g. easyroll1)
  3. Set a password and write it down — you'll enter this value in the blind's settings.
  4. Admin privileges are not required.

docs.title: ⑤ Check the MQTT integration
docs.text:
For the blind to talk to HA, the MQTT integration must be registered.

Go to Settings → Devices & Services → the [Integrations] tab at the top, then follow whichever of the three cases below matches your screen.

Case 1 — an MQTT card is already in the "Configured integrations" list at the bottom

It's already registered. You don't need to do anything. (Proceed to 2. Connecting the Device.)

Case 2 — MQTT appears under "Discovered integrations" at the top

Click the [Add] button on the card, then [Submit] in the window that follows to register it.

Case 3 — MQTT isn't anywhere (add it manually)

  1. Click [＋ Add Integration] at the bottom right of the screen.
  2. Type MQTT in the search box and select it.

  3. Enter the values below and click [Submit].

    Field Value Broker core-mosquitto Port 1883 Username / Password The MQTT account you created in ④

💡 Once registered, an MQTT card appears in the "Configured integrations" list.

💡 With that done, the blind is ready to connect. Continue to 2. Connecting the Device.

docs.title: 3 things to note down in advance
docs.text:
You'll need to enter these during the connection step, so write them down:

  1. Broker IP = the IP of the machine HA is installed on (e.g. 192.168.0.14)
    • Find it in HA: Settings → System → Network
    • 💡 Give the HA server a fixed IP (DHCP reservation on the router) — if its IP changes after a router swap or reboot, only the blinds' HA connection silently drops (app and device keep working). If it did change: for Hybrid, run [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again in the app; for HA-only, re-save the new IP on the device setup page. → 2. Connecting the Device · Good to know
  2. Broker port = 1883 by default
  3. MQTT username / password = the account you created above

⚠️ If you installed HA on a NAS virtual machine or similar, the IP must be the LAN IP visible on your router (not an internal address like 172.30.x.x).

docs.title: 2. Connecting the Device
docs.text:
There are two ways to connect to HA. Method ① Connect from the app (Hybrid) is recommended — it's the simplest to set up, and even if the internet goes down, HA can still control it locally, and even if HA is off you keep control via the app as long as the internet is connected.

Method How Result ① From the app ★Recommended Register the device in the EasyRoll app → [Home Assistant] in [Zone device settings] Hybrid: app + HA at the same time (independent of each other) ② Device setup page directly Type the device's IP into a browser and enter the HA info on the setup page Hybrid or HA only (no app control) — for use without the app / PC environments

ℹ️ The [Use as HomeAssistant] button that used to be on the app's start screen has been removed. In the app, register the device first, then connect HA from [Zone device settings] (Method ①).

Why is Method ① (Hybrid) recommended?

  • Double safety — Even if the internet goes down, HA can still control it locally, and even if HA is off you keep control via the app as long as the internet is connected. (The two connections are independent.)
  • Simple setup — register the device with the EasyRoll app, then connect several devices at once, per zone from the app's [Home Assistant] screen. Wrong input is reported immediately.
  • Keep all app features — alarms, schedules, member sharing and HA automations, together.
  • Requires firmware V3.2.0 or later (see the app's Device info → Firmware) → update via 7. Device Update

docs.title: Method ① Connect from the app — Hybrid (app + HA together) ★Recommended
docs.text:
From the EasyRoll app you connect several devices at once, per zone. If an entry is wrong, the device reports it before saving, so a failed attempt changes nothing.

ℹ️ The screenshots show the Korean app. On a phone set to English, the app shows the English labels used below; the Korean in parentheses matches the screenshots.

docs.title: Step 1 — Register the device with the EasyRoll app
docs.text:
If the device isn't registered in the app yet, register it first. Multiple devices can be done at once.

→ User Guide 2. Register Device · 2-1. Set Upper/Lower Limits

If you already use the device in the app, skip this step. If you just registered it, wait until the device shows Connected (연결됨, online) before continuing.

docs.title: Step 2 — Zone device settings → [Home Assistant]
docs.text:
1. On the main screen, tap ⚙ next to the zone name → [Zone device settings] (구역 기기 설정) → [Home Assistant] (Home Assistant 연결)
  2. Under Target blinds (대상 블라인드), select the devices to connect. To connect the whole zone, tap [Select all] (전체 선택).

  3. Enter the Home Assistant broker (Home Assistant 브로커 정보) details.

    Field Value Broker address (브로커 주소) IP of the HA machine (e.g. 192.168.0.14) Port (포트) 1883 Username / Password (계정 / 비밀번호) The MQTT account you created in Document 1

    💡 The password is stored on the device only — it is not kept in the app. Tap the 👁 icon to reveal what you typed.

    💡 The username in the screenshot (easyroll) is only an example. Enter the account you created in Document 1 (e.g. easyroll1).

  4. Tap [Connect] (연결하기) → on "Connect N blind(s) to Home Assistant?", tap [Confirm] (확인)

I can't see this menu, or it won't connect

  • It is shown only to the device owner (the account that registered it). Shared member accounts cannot connect to HA.
  • If the Home Assistant item in Device info shows Not supported on this device (지원하지 않는 기기), the firmware is below V3.2.0.
  • Even if it shows Not used (미사용), a device with firmware below V3.2.0 (V2.9.7–V3.1.x) cannot connect to HA, and the result ends in No response. Check Firmware in Device info.
  • In both cases, first update to V3.2.0 or later via 7. Device Update, then try again.

docs.title: Step 3 — Read the result
docs.text:
The device actually connects to the HA broker before saving (1–2 s). A result is shown for each device.

Shown Meaning What to do N of N applied (N대 중 N대 적용) · Done (완료) Verified → the device is restarting (about 1 min) Just wait Cannot reach (서버 연결 불가) Wrong broker address/port, or HA (the broker) is off Check the address, port and that the broker is running Login failed (계정 오류) MQTT account or password mismatch Check the account/password No response (응답 없음) The device didn't answer within 10 s (device off, or firmware below V3.2.0) Check device power/Wi-Fi and retry. If it keeps showing No response, check Firmware in Device info → if below V3.2.0, do 7. Device Update and retry

⚠️ Failed devices are left unchanged. Fix the input and simply try again.

On success, a Connected to Home Assistant (Home Assistant에 연결되었습니다) popup appears.

  • [Connect more] (추가 연결하기) — connect other devices in the same zone next. (The broker info is kept.)
  • [Back to home] (메인으로 돌아가기) — returns to the main screen.

💡 For devices in another zone, go back to the main screen and tap that zone's ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant]. You'll need to enter the broker info again. (The port is pre-filled with 1883.)

docs.title: Step 4 — Verify
docs.text:
• App: ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Device info] → if the Home Assistant item shows Connected (연결됨) with the broker/account, it worked. App control works as usual.
  • HA: the blind (EZS...) is registered automatically under Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT (about 1 min after the restart). → Verify the connection

💡 To disconnect from HA, select the devices on the same screen → [Disconnect from Home Assistant] (Home Assistant 연결 해제). The device goes back to app-only and its HA registration is cleaned up automatically. Afterwards the device info shows Not used (미사용).

docs.title: Method ② Open the device setup page directly (type the IP in a browser)
docs.text:
For environments where the app can't be used (PC only, or running with HA alone). Follow whichever matches the device's state.

ℹ️ The device's own setup pages are shown in Korean only. Below, each on-screen label is given in Korean, followed by its meaning in English.

docs.title: ②-A A device already registered in the app — http://<blind IP>:20318/hasetup
docs.text:
1. Find the blind's IP — EasyRoll app [Zone device settings] → [Device info] → Device IP
    • If the app can't show the IP (e.g. an HA-only device): look in your router's admin page, in the connected devices (DHCP) list, for a device whose name starts with EZS.
    • If an HA-only device is connected to HA, you can also send EZS_NETINFO$ from HA and read the ip: value in the /feedback reply. (How to send: 4. Advanced Commands)
  2. On a phone/PC on the same Wi-Fi, open http://<blind IP>:20318/hasetup in a browser (the Google Chrome browser is recommended)
  3. Enter the HA broker info in the HA_Server box: 브로커 IP (Broker IP) · 포트 (Port) 1883 · 사용자 (User) · 비밀번호 (Password). (Tap the 👁 icon to reveal the password.)
  4. Choose the mode you want.
    • Hybrid (app + HA) → ★ tick [Easyroll 앱과 함께 사용 (서버+HA 동시 연결)] ("Use with the Easyroll app") → [HA_Server로 전환·저장] (Switch to HA_Server · Save)
    • HA only (app control stops) → leave the box unticked → [HA_Server로 전환·저장]
  5. The device restarts and registers automatically in HA. (With Hybrid, the app keeps working too.)

The tick box decides the mode

Saving without the tick disconnects the app and makes it HA only. To keep using the app, be sure to tick the box. If that happened, press [Easyroll_Server로 복원] (Restore Easyroll_Server) on the same page and try again.

docs.title: Reverting to the EasyRoll app
docs.text:
When you want to disconnect from HA and go back to the EasyRoll app only, press one of the two buttons below.

Location Button .../20318/hasetup (same page) [Easyroll_Server로 복원] (Restore Easyroll_Server) Bottom of the .../20318/limitsetup page [Easyroll 모드로 전환] (Switch to Easyroll Mode)

⚠️ Unlike [Disconnect from Home Assistant] in the app, these two buttons do not remove the device's registration from HA. For a Hybrid device, the app's [Disconnect from Home Assistant] is the cleaner way (it also cleans up the HA registration automatically).

Device state after switching

  • A device that was registered in the EasyRoll app — works right away in the app after a few seconds.
  • A device that was never registered in the app — after a few minutes, the LED repeats "blink 3 times → pause 2 seconds". (Waiting-for-registration state.)
    • Do a device registration in the EasyRoll app to use it.
  • In HA — the device remains as "Unavailable". Open the blind (EZS...) under HA's Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT and delete it.
    • If you send EZS_HADISCOVERY_OFF$ from HA before switching, nothing is left behind in HA. → 4. Advanced Commands

docs.title: ②-B New device without the app (or a reset device) — 192.168.4.1 (HA only)
docs.text:
For running the blind with HA only, without using the EasyRoll app at all. The result is HA only (no app control).

⚠️ If you also want the app, use Method ① (register in the app, then connect) instead.

  1. Power ON the blind (a small movement and return means it's ready).
  2. On your phone/PC, connect to the blind's Wi-Fi name (EZS...) in Wi-Fi settings.
    • The password is u67184 + the last 3 characters of the device name (ID). e.g. if the device name is EZS...123, the password is u67184123
  3. Type 192.168.4.1 in your browser's address bar (the Google Chrome browser is recommended)

A setup screen like the one below appears. Follow the on-screen guidance to complete 상/하단 설정 (Upper/Lower Limit Setup) first, then choose a connection method.

docs.title: ②-B Step 4 — ⚙ 상/하단 설정 (Upper/Lower Limit Setup) — do this first
docs.text:
For the HA position slider (%) to work accurately, you must first tell the blind where its "top/bottom" are. On the home screen, tap [⚙ 상/하단 설정] (Upper/Lower Limit Setup).

Skip this if the motor's limits are already set

A device whose Upper/Lower limits were already set in the EasyRoll app has those values saved in the motor, so there's no need to set them again. Jump straight to ②-B Step 5 — Enter HA connection info.

  1. In 세팅모드 (Setup Mode), use ▲ 올림 / ▼ 내림 (Up/Down) to move to the top position you want → [상단 저장] (Save Upper)
    • ⚠️ 세팅모드 (Setup Mode) ignores saved limits and keeps moving. Be sure to press ■ 정지 (Stop) before it reaches the end.
  2. Move to the bottom position the same way → [하단 저장] (Save Lower) (order: Upper first → then Lower)
  3. Switch to 일반모드 (Normal Mode) and press ▲/▼ to confirm it stops properly at the saved positions.
  4. Use 짧게 이동 (jog) 1단계~4단계 (steps 1–4) for fine adjustment. (The larger the step, the more it moves.)
  5. If the direction is reversed, switch between 좌측 모터 / 우측 모터 (Left/Right motor) under 모터 방향 (Motor Direction). (Right by default; the device restarts when changed.)

💡 The 현재 위치 / 하단 (Current position / Lower, %) display on screen shows where it is right now.

💡 Even after registration, you can reconfigure anytime at http://<blind IP>:20318/limitsetup. (To find the blind's IP → ②-A step 1)

docs.title: ②-B Step 5 — Enter HA connection info
docs.text:
Once the limit setup is done, return to the home screen and tap [Home Assistant].

Section Fields 집 WiFi (Home Wi-Fi) SSID (Wi-Fi name) · 비밀번호 (Password) HA_Server 브로커 IP (Broker IP) · 포트 (Port, 1883) · 사용자 (User) · 비밀번호 (Password) ← the values you noted in Document 1

💡 Tap the 👁 icon in the password field to reveal what you typed.

Tap [저장하고 연결] (Save and Connect) and the device restarts, connecting automatically to your home Wi-Fi + HA.

It's normal for the screen to freeze or show 'Not connected' right after saving

When you save, the blind turns off its own Wi-Fi (EZS...) and moves to your home Wi-Fi. Because your phone/PC's connection to the device is dropped automatically, the browser page may not open or may look like an error. This is not a malfunction.

  • Reconnect your phone/PC's Wi-Fi to your usual home Wi-Fi.
  • Wait a moment (about 1 minute), then check Verify the connection below to see if it registered in HA.

Once connected, the blind registers automatically in HA. You don't need to press any extra Add button.

docs.title: Verify the connection
docs.text:
1. In HA: Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT → if the blind (EZS...) appears in the device list, it worked.
  2. Test movement with the ▲/▼/■ buttons on the device card.
  3. With Hybrid, also confirm it still works in the EasyRoll app as usual.

docs.title: Adding to the dashboard
docs.text: Connecting registers the device, but to make it visible on your dashboard (home screen) you need one more step. There are two ways — ① Assign an area is the simplest, and if you want to place it exactly where you like, use ② Add a card.

docs.title: ① Placing the device in the "Living Room" (recommended)
docs.text:
Putting a device in an area (room) lets HA's default dashboard organize it by room automatically.

  1. Settings → Devices & Services → the [Devices] tab at the top
  2. Select the blind (EZS...) from the list.
  3. Click the ⚙ (gear) or [Settings] on the device info card.
  4. Under Area, choose Living Room and click [Update].
    • If the room you want isn't there, type a name in the box to create a new one.
  5. Back on the dashboard, the blind appears inside the Living Room section.

💡 You can also rename the device here (e.g. EZS... → Living Room Blind). Pick a name that's easy to call in voice commands or automations.

docs.title: ② Adding it to the dashboard as a card
docs.text:
Use this when you want to place it in a specific spot on a specific dashboard.

  1. On the dashboard screen, click the ✏️ (pencil) at the top right to enter edit mode.
  2. Click [＋ Add Card].
  3. From the card types, pick Tile or Entities.
  4. In the Entity field, type cover. and select the blind. (e.g. cover.ezs16a4106036)
  5. [Save] → exit edit mode and the card is placed on the dashboard.

💡 The Tile card shows open/close/stop buttons in a single row and is the easiest to use.

💡 To put several blinds on one card, add multiple blinds to an Entities card.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• In Hybrid (Method ①, or Method ②-A with the box ticked), the EasyRoll app and HA are used at the same time. Even if the internet goes down, HA can still control it locally, and even if HA is off you keep control via the app as long as the internet is connected. (The two connections are independent.)
  • In HA only (Method ②-A unticked · ②-B), EasyRoll app control stops while connected to HA. (The remote and buttons always work in any mode.)
  • To connect or disconnect HA, use the app's [Home Assistant] screen: [Connect] / [Disconnect from Home Assistant]. (Without the app, use the device setup page .../20318/hasetup — if you revert from that page, you must delete the device in HA yourself.)
  • If the HA machine's IP changes, the blind can no longer reach HA. (The device keeps trying to reconnect.) Connect it again with the new address.
    • Hybrid — in the app, run ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again with the new broker address
    • HA only — open http://<blind IP>:20318/hasetup, enter the new broker IP and account info, and save again without the tick. Find the blind's IP in your router's connected devices list (②-A step 1). If you can't find the IP, do a factory reset (hold the button 5 seconds) and repeat ②-B from the start.
  • Doing a factory reset (hold the button 5 seconds) clears the HA settings and returns the device to its default (EasyRoll app) state. However, the device's registration in HA is not removed, so if you no longer use it in HA, delete the blind (EZS...) yourself under HA's Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT.

docs.title: 3. Using It in HA
docs.text: Once connected, HA automatically creates a cover entity + buttons.

docs.title: Device card
docs.text:
Control Action ▲ Open To the top ▼ Close To the bottom ■ Stop Halt Position slider Move to any % (100% = fully open, 0% = fully closed — HA standard) Jog up/down buttons Fine adjustment — hidden by default. Show them with EZS_HAJOG$ if needed (hide: EZS_HAJOG_OFF$, 4. Advanced Commands)

⚠️ To use the slider %, the device's Upper/Lower Limit Setup must be done. Without it, only 0/100 work. (How to set it: User Guide 2-1. Set Upper/Lower Limits — for HA-only devices without the app, see 2. Connecting the Device ②-B Step 4 or http://<blind IP>:20318/limitsetup)

docs.title: Online/offline status
docs.text:
• If the device loses power or its connection drops, HA shows it as "Unavailable" (after about 1–3 minutes on a Hybrid device, or about 15–45 seconds on an HA-only device).
  • When it comes back on, it automatically returns to "Available".

docs.title: Automation examples
docs.text:
Use it in HA automations just like any other cover.

# e.g. Close the living room blind 30 min after sunset
automation:
  - alias: "Close blinds at sunset"
    trigger:
      - platform: sun
        event: sunset
        offset: "00:30:00"
    action:
      - service: cover.close_cover
        target:
          entity_id: cover.ezs16a4______

# e.g. Open to 70% at 7 AM
      - service: cover.set_cover_position
        target:
          entity_id: cover.ezs16a4______
        data:
          position: 70

docs.title: 4. Advanced Commands (Direct MQTT Control)
docs.text: If the card buttons are enough for you, you can skip this chapter. This is for advanced users who need detailed configuration or diagnostics.

docs.title: Where to send commands
docs.text: Go to Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT → ⚙ Configure (on the Mosquitto row) and you can use the two tools below.

docs.title: Sending a command — Publish a packet
docs.text: Field Value Topic /<device ID> — e.g. /EZS16A4106036 Payload The command to send — e.g. EZS_5U0$

docs.title: Viewing responses — Listen to a topic
docs.text:
Field Value Topic # (listen to everything)

💡 Responses reach HA only from HA-only devices. Most come up on the /feedback topic, and the firmware version (EZS_VER$) on /version/<device ID>.

💡 On a Hybrid (app + HA) device, replies to query commands go to the EasyRoll server, so they don't appear in HA. Check the version and status in the EasyRoll app under ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Device info]. The position is still reflected on the HA card and on /<device ID>/pos.

docs.title: Command rules
docs.text:
Every command starts with EZS_

Commands sent from HA must always start with EZS_.

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text: Command Action EZS_5U0$ / EZS_5D0$ / EZS_5S0$ Open / Close / Stop EZS_AL050.000$ Move to a given % position — 000.000 = top (fully open) – 100.000 = bottom (fully closed). This is the opposite of the HA slider % (e.g. HA 70% open = EZS_AL030.000$) EZS_POS$ Query current position — pct in the reply and the /<device ID>/pos value use the same scale (0 = top) EZS_VER$ Query firmware version — reply topic /version/<device ID> EZS_RSS$ Query Wi-Fi signal strength (useful for diagnosing connection issues) EZS_5G1$ ~ EZS_5G4$ Move to saved positions 1–4 EZS_5g1$ ~ EZS_5g4$ Save the current position to 1–4 EZS_HADISCOVERY$ Re-register the device in HA (when entities have disappeared) EZS_HADISCOVERY_OFF$ Remove the device's registration from HA EZS_MQTTINFO$ Query the current connection info — on an HA-only device: mode:ha, broker address, port and username (password excluded) EZS_HAJOG$ / EZS_HAJOG_OFF$ Show / hide the jog (short up/down) buttons on the HA card (hidden by default)

docs.title: Stuck at the connection step
docs.text: Symptom Check EZS... doesn't appear in the Wi-Fi list Reconnect power and wait 1 minute. If it's an already-registered device, hold the button 5 seconds (reset) and retry 192.168.4.1 won't open Make sure your phone is connected to the device Wi-Fi (EZS...) (not your home Wi-Fi). Turn off mobile data briefly Saved, but the device doesn't show up in HA ① Are the blind and HA on the same router? ② Any typo in the broker IP/port/account? ③ Is the Mosquitto add-on running? No MQTT integration at all Add the MQTT integration in HA + install the Mosquitto add-on first (1. Requirements)

docs.title: Problems during use
docs.text: Symptom Check Card exists but shows "Unavailable" Check the device power/Wi-Fi. If the device LED blinks at 3-second intervals, it's reconnecting — wait a moment. On a Hybrid device where the app still works, see App works but HA doesn't below Slider only does 0/100 The device's Upper/Lower Limit Setup isn't done — it works normally after setup (2-1. Set Upper/Lower Limits; for devices without the app, ②-B Step 4) Entity disappeared Send EZS_HADISCOVERY$ to re-register (4. Advanced Commands) No response when sending a command Check that the command starts with EZS_ and the topic is /<device ID> App works but HA doesn't (Hybrid) Check that the HA broker (Mosquitto) is running and that the HA machine's IP hasn't changed. The device keeps retrying, so it recovers automatically once the broker is back. If the IP changed, run ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again in the app with the new address (a fixed IP for the HA server is recommended) HA doesn't work (HA-only) — the HA machine's IP changed Re-save on http://<blind IP>:20318/hasetup with the new broker IP and without the checkbox. How to find the blind's IP, and the reset route, are in 2. Connecting the Device · Good to know HA works but the app doesn't (Hybrid) Check the internet (router WAN) connection. It recovers automatically once the internet is back — meanwhile you can still control via HA No [Home Assistant] menu under [Zone device settings] in the app It is shown only to the device owner account (shared member accounts can't see it). Also make sure the app is up to date Device info shows "Not supported on this device" Firmware below V3.2.0 → do 7. Device Update and retry Result shows "Cannot reach" / "Login failed" / "No response" In order: check broker address, port and that the broker is running / check the MQTT account and password / check device power and Wi-Fi — "No response" also appears when the firmware is below V3.2.0 (the Home Assistant item in Device info shows "Not used"). Check the firmware in [Device info] and do 7. Device Update, then retry. Failed devices are left unchanged, so fix the input and retry

docs.title: What happens to the device when HA (the broker) goes down?
docs.text:
Even if the broker briefly disappears due to a NAS reboot, HA update, etc., there's nothing to worry about:

  • The device keeps trying to reconnect automatically, and reconnects on its own when the broker returns.
  • Meanwhile, the remote and buttons still work normally.
  • On an HA-only device, if the LED blinks once every 3 seconds, that indicates "reconnecting."
  • On a Hybrid (app + HA) device, the LED doesn't change when HA goes down, and you keep control via the app. (On a Hybrid device, the 3-second blink means it is reconnecting to the internet (server).)

docs.title: I changed my Wi-Fi router
docs.text:
If you only changed the router, there's no need to reset — just wait for the device to return to setup mode (AP) on its own.

Wait 1–2 minutes until an EZS... network reappears in your phone's Wi-Fi list. (Don't unplug it — a power cycle restarts the attempts and makes it take longer.)

  • Hybrid (app + HA) device — just set the new Wi-Fi with the EasyRoll app's Changing the Wi-Fi Router. The saved HA settings stay, so it reconnects to HA as well. (If the HA machine's IP also changed with the new router, only HA silently drops — run [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again in the app with the new address. A fixed IP for the HA server is recommended.)
  • HA-only device — connect to that EZS... Wi-Fi → open 192.168.4.1 in a browser → [Home Assistant] → enter the new home Wi-Fi + HA broker info → [저장하고 연결] (Save and Connect) (for the fields, see Method ②-B in 2. Connecting the Device)

💡 ★Upper/lower limits and the current position are kept in every case, so no need to set the limits again.

docs.title: I deleted the device from HA and now the LED is blinking
docs.text:
On an HA-only device, if you delete the device's account from HA (Mosquitto), the device is refused a connection and enters Setup Mode (LED blinks 3 times).

  • To use it again: restore the account and wait a moment for it to return automatically, or re-set it up via Method ②-B in 2. Connecting the Device.
  • To go back to the EasyRoll app: hold the device button 5 seconds (reset), then register in the EasyRoll app.

On a Hybrid (app + HA) device, deleting the HA account doesn't change the LED or put it into Setup Mode — only the HA connection drops, and the app keeps working.

  • To use HA again: restore the account and it reconnects automatically. To use a different account, run ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] again in the app. (No reset or ②-B setup is needed — saving via ②-B would switch the device to HA only.)

💡 To move it to another home/HA: for a Hybrid device, simply delete the device in the app and it disappears from HA automatically. For an HA-only device, use EZS_HARESET$ → Move / Remove Device (V3.2.0 or later)

docs.title: I want to revert to the EasyRoll app
docs.text:
• Hybrid device: in the app, ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] → select the devices → [Disconnect from Home Assistant]
  • HA-only device: [Easyroll_Server로 복원] (Restore Easyroll_Server) on the device setup page http://<blind IP>:20318/hasetup — or reset the device (hold the button 5 s) and register it in the app
    • Neither of these removes the device from HA. Delete the blind (EZS...) yourself in HA under Settings → Devices & services → MQTT. (Details)

docs.title: If it still doesn't work
docs.text:
Customer Center 031-358-1016 · Weekdays 09:00 – 18:00

Website easyroll.kr · Community → Q&A board

When contacting us, please include the device ID (EZS...), the LED state, and the firmware version (EasyRoll app [Zone device settings] → [Device info] → Firmware — for an HA-only device, the EZS_VER$ response).

docs.title: Moving / Removing a Device
docs.text:
How to move a device that was connected to HA to another home, router or HA, or remove it cleanly from HA. The procedure depends on the connection mode — a Hybrid (app + HA) device only needs to be deleted in the app, while an HA-only device is reset with a single command.

Firmware required — V3.2.0 or later

The procedures below (automatic HA cleanup on app deletion, EZS_HARESET$) work on firmware V3.2.0 or later. Check the version in the app under [Zone device settings] → [Device info] → Firmware, or with the EZS_VER$ command (HA-only devices). If it's lower, update first via 7. Device Update.

docs.title: Hybrid (app + HA) device — just delete it in the app
docs.text:
1. In the EasyRoll app, tap ⚙ next to the zone name → [Delete device] → select the blinds to remove (select all of them to clear the zone) → [Delete selected] → [Confirm] (the screenshot shows the Korean app)
  2. The device receives the deletion notice, cleans up its HA registration by itself, clears its Wi-Fi/HA settings and restarts → it returns to setup AP mode (EZS... Wi-Fi).
  3. The device disappears from HA within seconds (no ghost "unavailable" device is left behind).

💡 If the device was powered off at the moment of deletion, it cleans itself up within 3–4 minutes after it is next powered on.

💡 If you only want to disconnect HA and keep using the app, use Disconnect from Home Assistant instead of deleting.

docs.title: Reconnecting at the new location
docs.text: Since the device is back in AP mode, simply start over with Method ① in 2. Connecting the Device: register the device with the EasyRoll app (new Wi-Fi) → ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] and enter the new HA broker info.

docs.title: HA-only device — EZS_HARESET$
docs.text:
A device used with HA only (never registered in the app) is reset with a single command from HA. (Use the same command when you want to move a device while keeping its server registration.)

If you sent it to a device that was registered in the app

The server-side registration is not removed, so the device stays in the app as 'offline'. (For a Hybrid device, simply deleting it in the app is the easier route.) On a Hybrid device, the ha_reset:ok reply in step 2 below goes to the EasyRoll server and doesn't appear in HA, but you can still see the device disappear from HA and restart.

  • To keep using it in the same home: connect to the device Wi-Fi (EZS...) and re-enter just the router info to bring it back to the app → reconnect HA with ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] in the app
  • To move it to another site: also delete the device in the app

Send the command from the same place as in 4. Advanced Commands — "Where to send commands".

In HA, commands start with EZS_, not #

It's EZS_HARESET$, not #HARESET$.

  1. In HA, go to Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT → ⚙ Configure → Publish a packet and send:

    Field Value Topic /<device ID> — e.g. /EZS16J1234567 Payload EZS_HARESET$

  2. The device replies with ha_reset:ok on /feedback, then restarts automatically a few seconds later.

  3. After restarting, the device disappears cleanly from HA and returns to setup AP mode (EZS... Wi-Fi).

docs.title: Reconnecting at the new location
docs.text:
• Switch to Hybrid ★Recommended — register the device with the EasyRoll app → ⚙ → [Zone device settings] → [Home Assistant] (Method ①)
  • Stay HA only — connect your phone to the device Wi-Fi (EZS...) → open 192.168.4.1 in a browser → [Home Assistant] → enter the new home Wi-Fi + new HA broker info → [저장하고 연결] (Save and Connect) (Method ②-B)

Upper/lower limits and the current position are NOT erased

Both app deletion and EZS_HARESET$ clear only the Wi-Fi/HA connection info. The upper/lower positions stored in the motor are kept, so you don't need to set the limits again after reinstalling.

docs.title: Comparison — which method should I use?
docs.text: Situation Method Connection Limit settings Temporarily hide from the HA screen EZS_HADISCOVERY_OFF$ Kept (restore anytime with EZS_HADISCOVERY$) Kept Drop HA but keep the app (Hybrid) App [Disconnect from Home Assistant] Switches to app only; HA registration cleaned up automatically Kept Move to another home/HA — Hybrid device Delete the device in the app Cleared → back to AP mode; HA cleaned up automatically Kept Move to another home/HA — HA-only device EZS_HARESET$ Cleared → back to AP mode Kept Full factory reset Hold device button 5s Cleared → default (EasyRoll app) state Kept

docs.title: SmartThings Integration
docs.text:
Works With SmartThings certified

The EasyRoll Smart Blind (EasyRoll Smartblind) is an officially certified partner device that has passed Samsung's WWST (Works With SmartThings) certification. It connects right in the SmartThings app — no separate hub needed, just your Samsung account and EasyRoll account — and Bixby and Routines (automations) are fully supported.

Connect your EasyRoll Smart Blind to Samsung SmartThings to control it alongside your Galaxy phone and Samsung appliances on one screen, and operate it with Bixby voice as well.

docs.title: Features covered by the certification
docs.text:
Feature In SmartThings Open · Close · Stop Close · Pause · Open buttons on the device card / Bixby / Routines Position % Set any height with the slider (100% = fully open, 0% = fully closed — SmartThings convention) Preset positions m1 · m2 · m3 Tap ◎ on the card to move to a preset height in one go; change the height with ⚙ (initially 25% / 50% / 75%) Live status Opening / Closing / Open / Closed / Partially open — the card updates automatically as the blind moves Online / Offline If the blind loses power or internet, SmartThings shows it as "offline"

💡 In the screenshot, the m1 · m2 · m3 values 42 / 65 / 85 are examples changed with ⚙. When you first connect, they start at 25 / 50 / 75.

💡 The SmartThings presets m1 · m2 · m3 are separate from the M1–M3 memory positions in the EasyRoll app. Set each up as you like.

docs.title: What You'll Need
docs.text:
• An account with your blind registered in the EasyRoll app (Register Device completed)
  • Connect with the account that registered (owns) the blinds — blinds shared with you as a member are not linked.
  • The SmartThings app installed on your smartphone + signed in with your Samsung account
  • The blind connected to the internet (home Wi-Fi) — the SmartThings integration works through the EasyRoll server

docs.title: Connecting (One-Time Setup)
docs.text:
1. SmartThings app → [+ Add Device] → [Add] under Partner devices

  2. Select EasyRoll SmartBlind from the brand list (type "EasyRoll" in the 🔍 search box to jump straight to it)

    ⚠️ A similarly named EasyRoll (the older integration) also appears in the list. For a new connection, be sure to pick EasyRoll SmartBlind (the certified version).

  3. When the EasyRoll login page opens, sign in with your EasyRoll app account (email and password)

  4. When your registered blinds appear in the SmartThings [Devices] tab automatically, you're done!

    💡 Blinds arrive with names in the form "[Inoshade] number(zone name)" — e.g. "[Inoshade] 1(Living Room)" — and are first placed under "No room assigned". Use ⋮ at the top right of the device screen to give each one an easy-to-say name such as "Living Room Blind" and assign it to a room (e.g. Living Room), so Bixby voice and Routines recognize it more reliably.

💡 All blinds registered in the EasyRoll app are added to SmartThings at once (only blinds registered to your own account — shared blinds are not included). Blinds you register later are added to SmartThings automatically as well (this can take up to about a day).

💡 If you connected to SmartThings earlier, you can keep using that connection as is.

docs.text:
Symptom Solution EasyRoll SmartBlind isn't in the list The list is alphabetical — scroll to E or type "EasyRoll" in the 🔍 search box → if it's still missing, update the SmartThings app to the latest version and try again Connected but the device doesn't show Check that you signed in with the owner account that registered the blinds (blinds shared with you as a member don't appear) → check in the EasyRoll app that the blind is properly registered and online. A newly registered blind can take up to about a day to appear in SmartThings Card controls don't respond Check that the blind is online (FAQ) → disconnect the SmartThings link and reconnect The position % in SmartThings differs from the app SmartThings uses the same convention as the EasyRoll app (100% = fully open), so the values should match.
